correctness.rationale: Uniform edge ranks can be represented by iid rate-1/n exponential clocks. The first incident edge at each vertex is exactly what the unseen-endpoint rule retains, so components are born at size two and never merge. Every edge touching an unseen vertex is unrevealed; residual memorylessness gives state-changing rates u(u−1)/(2n) for births and uj/n for adding to each size-j component. Counting deletions of unseen vertices yields drift −(n−1)Z_n/n and the stated triangular size drifts. On [0,T], the jump bound and the total rate at most n/2 give quadratic variation O(T/n); Doob and the Lipschitz drift comparison give uniform-in-probability fluid convergence, hence bounded-coordinate L1 convergence. The two-ancestor birth law with generating function [p r/(1−(1−p)r)]² solves the limiting growth equations with p=exp(−e^(−s)+e^(−t)); integrating the immigration rate e^(−2s)/2, then substituting u=e^(−s) at t=∞, yields the claimed c_k. Each late state change consumes a previously unseen vertex, whose mean fraction is e^(−(n−1)T/n), so taking n→∞ before T→∞ is justified. Direct integrations for k=2,3 give the displayed constants; geometric summation gives total density 1/4 and vertex mass ∫_0^1 u e^u du=1. Coordinate convergence and that mass identity control the vertex tail; the component-count tail is always bounded by 1/(K+1). These prove both conditional total-variation limits in probability, the total component-count limit, and no component of linear size.
